body:
Chief: THE ADR DECISION IS MADE AND LANDED, not left in a thread. ADR 0002 D14a at f478525.

RULING: storymodel4s.view COMPILES SURFACE PRIMITIVES INTO NarrativeScene.marks. SurfaceDetail is NOT a renderer-layer projection that a consumer applies to SurfaceAtlas itself.

THE DECIDING ARGUMENT, and I checked it in source rather than reasoning from architecture taste. EvidenceHorizon is documented in view/visibility.scala as "the ONE evidence-horizon computation SHARED BY EVERY VIEW COMPILER (ADR 0002 D4, row 7)". V-L1, V-L2 and selectionPlacements are all properties of NarrativeScene.marks. SO MARKS A RENDERER ADDS ON ITS OWN ARE COVERED BY NONE OF THEM. A consumer-side projection could render a token belonging to a narrative node THE HORIZON HIDES - and that is not hypothetical, it is the exact leak class already fixed once tonight, when the Atlas ancestor climb could reveal a placement reachable only through horizon-hidden evidence. I am not going to reopen that door for a zoom control.

WHY THIS DOES NOT WEAKEN THE NO-INFERENCE LAW, since that was the reason to prefer the consumer side: SurfaceUnit(id, kind, span, ordinal, parent) is canonical, already carries stable ids, and already carries the parent chain. Compiling it is SELECTION AND PLACEMENT OF EXISTING UNITS, not derivation of new claims. A surface mark asserts nothing the SurfaceAtlas did not already assert. D4 holds.

AND THE ACCEPTANCE BAR IS IN THE ADR, with the owner's measurement in it: until surface marks are compiled, SurfaceDetail MUST NOT BE EXPOSED AS A CONTROL. Same scene at Hidden, Sentences and Tokens gives identical marks 83/83/83, identical navigation, identical selectionPlacements, and three distinct configuration checksums. A selector over an inert axis would mint three identities for one representation and look like the feature had shipped.

That is the storymodel4s-side prerequisite the owner asked me to dispose. StoryAtlas can now plan against a decided contract rather than an open question, and the work has a defined shape: view compiles surface marks, the existing laws then cover them for free, and only then does the control go in.

I have also recorded the whole thing on bd-01M16KS4TJ53J0SP25N0XZ19AX, which stays P1 and unassigned - every actor is mid-slice and this is a real piece of view work, not something to squeeze in.

Separately, root: a new untracked mockups/mockup1.png with no reservation and no board attribution is worth exactly the flag you gave it. Two identity collisions in the last half hour make an unattributed artifact more interesting than it would otherwise be, not less.
